studies.label: Wave 1 lab experiment (HI vs HAT vs HHT), picture-idea tasks 2 and 3
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Robust SEs clustered by experimental session. The counts are observed session clusters in Table D.2 (PDF p. 19), not confirmation of session randomization. Assignment of individuals versus sessions is unresolved (PDF pp. 2 and 6). Each person attended one main session, so session clustering encompasses their repeated outputs.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 19, Table D.2, columns Training, HAT, HI, HHT
counts_source.quote: In the ﬁrst wave, 246 participants were recruited and randomly assigned to one of three between-subject treatments. ... Training HAT HI HHT ... No. subjects 56 61 63 122 No. sessions 2 2 2 5

arms.name: HI (Control)
arms.description: Works alone without ChatGPT in the treated picture-idea tasks.

arms.name: HAT
arms.description: Works individually with ChatGPT 3.5 through poe.com in the treated picture-idea tasks.

arms.name: HHT
arms.description: Anonymous human pairs, randomly rematched for each treated task, submit one joint idea.

studies.task: Write creative picture ideas for the counterbalanced here and new-skill themes; experimenters subsequently render the text as images for creativity evaluation.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT 3.5 via poe.com
ai_tool.locator: PDF pp. 4 and 6, Sections 2.1 and 2.3. The release year is not stated; study dates are not used as release dates.

preregistration.where: AsPredicted.org; PDF p. 6 points to preregistration and deviations in Supplementary Section 1, unavailable.

studies.shared_sample: Wave-1 participants were reported with earlier ratings in Zhu and Zou (2023), The role of generative AI in human creative processes: experimental evidence, SSRN 4676053 (PDF p. 2, footnote 2; PDF p. 22). Same sample, earlier paper version.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Mean creativity rating on a 1 to 10 scale, with one decimal, from 30 blind student evaluators per theme. Evaluators saw the submitted picture-idea text and an image generated from it by the experimenters using DALL-E 3.

regression.model: Table 3 column (2), random-effects grade model with session-clustered robust SEs and theme and task-order indicators. Adds the unbalanced baseline covariates: major, belief that AI replaces humans in creativity, and prior generative-AI use. Other arm indicators include HHT and nonrandomized Training.

paper_effect.standardizer: Regression coefficient divided by the SD of the outcome variable (Appendix C); its aggregation and relationship to a control-arm or pooled participant SD are unspecified. Not coded as Cohen d or Hedges g.

estimates.notes: Analyzed people counts for this contrast are not explicitly printed. Allocations, submissions, and regression rows are not substituted for analyzed people. n_units is the printed model-row count across all included arms, including Training, not people or the size of this two-arm contrast. HHT outputs are expanded to one row per team member. Robust SEs are clustered by session. Each participant attended one main session (PDF p. 6), so this clustering encompasses all their repeated outputs; se_basis is participant on that basis. Individual versus session randomization remains unresolved. If sessions were randomized, se_basis must be cluster. Table 2 labels the parenthesized values SDs but does not establish their aggregation level sufficiently for participant standardization; sd_level is null. The arm means and SDs are unadjusted Table 2 summaries; the regression coefficient is adjusted. The manuscript names image-text grades primary and emphasizes this specification; the unavailable preregistration prevents confirming preregistered primary status.

not_extracted.what: S2: all Training comparisons with HAT, HI, or HHT
not_extracted.reason: A separately recruited later cohort, with timing and selection differences. The authors reject a rigorous causal interpretation of Training versus HAT (PDF pp. 3 and 5); the blanket random-distribution wording in Appendix B.2 does not resolve this.

not_extracted.what: S3: standalone ChatGPT and mechanically constructed hypothetical-team benchmarks
not_extracted.reason: An arm has no person working, or consists of mechanically selected outputs, rather than randomized assistance to people (PDF p. 12; Tables D.4-D.5, PDF p. 20). Human-arm means in those tables are retained separately, without model-only results or benchmark significance stars.

AI availability during the test is unstated (PDF pp. 4 and 16); with_ai versus after_ai cannot be classified. Figure 4b has no numerical coefficient or CI endpoints (PDF p. 11). The text reports no statistically significant effect (PDF p. 12).

AI availability during the test is unstated (PDF pp. 4 and 16); with_ai versus after_ai cannot be classified. PDF p. 12 prints: "experiencing ChatGPT access and experiencing teamwork both lead to an increase of 0.19 SDs in the modiﬁed-DAT score". This printed 0.19 SD result is preserved for reconciliation; raw coefficients, SEs, CI endpoints, and arm levels are not printed. No graph coordinates were read.

not_extracted.what: Table 7 columns (2)-(4) and (6)-(8), supplementary Tables S9-S10
not_extracted.reason: Effects adjusted for post-treatment overlap or keyword-origin mediators (PDF p. 13). Baseline columns without mediators are retained.

not_extracted.what: Table 3 full-control columns (3) and (6), and Table D.3
not_extracted.reason: The full-control models include prior drawing-AI experience, which Appendix A.2 says was collected in the final Questionnaire III (PDF pp. 8, 16 and 20). Omitted under the rule against adjustment for variables measured after treatment, even though the question concerns prior experience. Table D.3 interaction columns also report moderation.
Neither arm receives AI assistance during the scored tasks; HHT is retained only as an active comparator for HAT.

The initial task is unassisted for everyone; final-task assistance depends on preferences and the BDM procedure. No eligible full-sample randomized output contrast is printed for those tasks (PDF pp. 2, 4 and 16).

not_extracted.reason: Compares evaluation formats and evaluators, not randomized AI assistance to people (PDF p. 21).

Referenced at PDF p. 8 but absent from the saved PDF and local files. Python urllib requests to the named Elsevier Article Retrieval API and article DOI both failed with socket permission errors; no supplementary values inferred.

open_items: Resolve individual versus session allocation. assignment_unit is null; clusters_per_arm holds observed session counts only (PDF pp. 2, 6 and 19).
SEs encompass repeated participant observations through session clustering. Participant versus randomized-cluster coding remains dependent on the allocation protocol.

Obtain explicitly printed analyzed people counts by arm and outcome. Appendix B.2 supplies exclusions but no resulting counts, so screening-form counts derived by subtraction are not copied. Image failures and missing grades add outcome-specific gaps (PDF p. 17).
Identify the aggregation of Table 2 SDs and the outcome SD used for the printed standardized coefficient (PDF pp. 7-8 and 18).
Obtain the supplementary preregistration, deviations, allocation protocol, DAT instructions, and robustness tables (PDF pp. 6, 8 and 21).
Confirm AI access during post-treatment DATs before classifying with_ai versus after_ai; obtain exact coefficients, SEs, arm levels, and analyzed counts (PDF pp. 4, 11-12, 16-18).
Identify Table 5 grade format and aggregation, and obtain uncertainty estimates (PDF p. 10).

The main adjusted models label major, AI-replacement belief, and AI-use experience baseline controls. Major is demographic information collected in Questionnaire III; this timing should be reviewed under a literal application of the post-treatment measurement rule. Unadjusted Table 3 models remain available.

Theme-specific human-arm summaries in Tables D.4-D.5 have no explicit human-arm contrast uncertainty; significance stars compare each group with standalone ChatGPT and are not transferred to the extracted human-arm comparisons.
notes: Read the entire markdown sequentially, including appendices and references, and checked cited PDF text with pymupdf. Only the randomized first wave is a study here. Pooled regressions include Training, but only randomized wave-1 coefficients are extracted. No statistics, counts, or intervals are computed; no unlabeled figure coordinates are transcribed. Source quotes preserve printed precision and signs, including negative zero. All n_analyzed and contrast people counts are null when not directly printed. Each participant first familiarized themselves with ChatGPT, including Control and HHT (PDF p. 4). Main-task arm comparisons are between subjects, not a randomized crossover. The manuscript emphasizes image-text grading and Table 3 column (2); s1_image_creativity_hat_vs_hi_main is its main reported specification (PDF pp. 6-7), with preregistered status unresolved. Multiple specifications and descriptive contrasts reuse participants. No other extractor file or web search was used.
